research_note: THE HUNTOON PLACE, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: 'The northwest quarter of this large block of ground was known as the "Huntoon Place," having the appearance of a large country farm-house. The residence stood well back from the street, and the lot was filled with large trees. The house was a landmark, having been built by Judge J. D. Caton, nearly half a century before. The quaint old mansion had twelve stacks of chimneys ... a picturesque place in a neighborhood of puffing and impertinent modern factories' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717). No picture of it is known.
